description: Checks the file uploaded to an `upload_media` target and makes it usable. Returns the media `url` to pass to other tools, the file's size, its `kind` (`video` or `image`), its measured `width` and `height` and, for a video, `duration_seconds`. WHEN: right after the bytes moved (the curl printed a 2xx, or the user says they finished on the `browser_upload_url` page). It checks that the CONTENTS match the declared type and that the media is MEASURABLE (every later transform is priced from the measurement). A file that fails is refused and never added, and nothing is charged: re-encode to MP4, PNG or JPEG. IF IT SAYS NOTHING HAS BEEN UPLOADED YET, the bytes did not land. Curl route: read the body it printed (S3's own reason; a bare `000` means your environment cannot reach the storage host, so switch to `browser_upload_url`). Browser route: the user has probably not finished. DO NOT CALL `upload_media` AGAIN (the first target lives its whole 15 minutes): say in one line that you are waiting, without the link, and call this again when they say they are done. If the upload reported success, a CDN may serve a cached miss: wait a few seconds and call once more. Costs no tokens; safe to call again on the same id. AFTER THIS the `url` works anywhere its kind is taken: a VIDEO as `source_video` (`upscale_video`, `extend_video`), `reference_video` (`motion_control`) or in `reference_videos` (`generate_video`); an IMAGE as `source_image` (`upscale_image`), `character_image` (`generate_lipsync`, `motion_control`), a start, end or reference image on `generate_video`, or an input on `generate_image`.
name: confirm_upload
title: Finish an upload started by upload_media
